All notable changes to Memento-Skills are documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project aspires to follow [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **Phase 3 candidate #6 closure — `doc-generator` and `release-notes` Phase-1 criterion met (`docs/api/skill-retrieval.md`, `docs/release-notes-unreleased-draft.md`, `docs/analysis/candidate-6-cycle-closure.md`)** — **docs-only; no source code or test-suite changes shipped.** Per the Phase 3 interim retrospective's ordering, the two tech-writing skills still flagged as "needs ≥ 2 create → test → review → improve cycles with revisions" were driven through two cycles each against real inputs. (a) **`doc-generator`** against `core/skill/retrieval/` (8 files, 8 classes, 50 methods; 30 docstrings flagged non-target or mixed-script by the translation-summary mode) produced `docs/api/skill-retrieval.md` — covers the `RecallCandidate` schema including MS-DES-0004 `bm25_score`/`vector_score`/`bm25_rank`/`vector_rank` additions, the `BaseRecall` protocol, four concrete strategies, and the `MultiRecall` fusion coordinator with RRF math, tier rule, and merge semantics. Cycle 1b surfaced **five findings** (header-hierarchy bug putting `MultiRecall` under "Concrete strategies"; missing explanation for `LocalFileRecall.search(k=0)` and `RemoteRecall.search(k=5)` divergence from the `BaseRecall` `k=10` default; self-contradictory "silently dropped … metadata breadcrumb stashed" merge bullet; overreach on the "port to `doc_importance.py`" claim; plus a `RRF_K=60` duplicate-constant tech-debt observation left unfixed). Cycle 2a applied four revisions. (b) **`release-notes`** against the nine-entry `[Unreleased]` window produced `docs/release-notes-unreleased-draft.md`, clearly labeled **DRAFT / not a version stamp** — no `pyproject.toml` edit was performed, and the file will be regenerated and renamed when the real cut happens. Cycle 1b surfaced one finding (summary claimed "eight substantive changes" vs. the actual nine); cycle 2a corrected the count and explicitly named the two non-MS-DES items (the `Market` PROPER_NOUNS widening and the `current_warnings_backlog` accessor correction) plus the standalone style-guide meta-fix sweep. Style-checker was clean on **all four artifact+cycle combinations** — partial evidence that MS-DES-0007 Rule 3.1 hardening and MS-DES-0010 `Market` widening are doing their job on freshly-authored prose (the single finding, a mid-heading "Phase 1" in the findings note's H1, was corrected by reword per the existing `docs/phase-3-interim-retrospective.md:90` precedent rather than by widening `PROPER_NOUNS` — widening `phase` would silently re-uppercase legitimate lowercase `phase N` occurrences elsewhere). Findings trail with Phase-1 closure statement captured at [`docs/analysis/candidate-6-cycle-closure.md`](docs/analysis/candidate-6-cycle-closure.md). Closes Phase 3 candidate #6 from the interim retrospective. Remaining Phase 3 work: MS-DES-0011 (remote BM25 implementation, gated on Market-owner decision), translation-pass backlog on `core/skill/retrieval/`, and the `RRF_K` duplicate-constant consolidation observation.
- **Remote BM25 fusion design-space spec (`docs/design/remote-bm25-fusion.md`, MS-DES-0010)** — **docs-only; no client-side or server-side code shipped in this cycle.** Phase 3 candidate #4 was flagged by the interim retrospective as "not next" because the blocking question — *"does the Market have a BM25 index surface?"* — is a cross-system design decision that needs sign-off from whoever owns the `skill_retrieval_api` service. Rather than invent a Market-side schema to unblock ourselves (which would violate the user's "do not make up undocumented features" standing preference), this MS-DES enumerates the three plausible surface shapes — (A) `strategy` parameter on the existing `/api/v1/search` endpoint, (B) sibling `/api/v1/search_bm25` endpoint, (C) multi-field response shape returning per-strategy `bm25_score`/`bm25_rank`/`vector_score`/`vector_rank` — walks through the concrete client-side deltas each would require in `RemoteRecall`, `MultiRecall._stamp_rank`/`_apply_fusion`, and `RecallCandidate`, and locks in five rejected alternatives (dual-remote client shim; use remote `score` as a BM25 proxy; drop the local-before-remote tier rule; mirror the remote catalog locally; wait indefinitely). Six open questions are tagged for Market-owner resolution — including fan-out capacity, a `bm25_ready` health signal analogous to today's `embedding_ready`, and the question of whether remote-BM25 and local-BM25 should fuse as one merged signal or as two independent terms in the RRF sum. The spec follows the house-style MS-DES-NNNN format so it slots alongside MS-DES-0003 through MS-DES-0009 without stylistic friction and its own acceptance criteria are explicitly about the spec itself (not yet-unwritten code). Conditional recommendation in the doc: Shape C is lowest long-run client complexity if the Market team owns both sides and can ship a breaking schema rev; Shape A is the minimum-invasiveness path otherwise. A follow-up MS-DES-0011 will nail down the implementation once a shape is chosen. Closes the docs-first half of Phase 3 candidate #4; implementation deferred until open question 1 is resolved.
- **`Market` added to `PROPER_NOUNS` (`skills/style-checker/scripts/style_autofix.py`, `skills/style-checker/scripts/test_style_autofix.py`)** — surfaced while style-cleaning MS-DES-0010. Throughout MS-DES-0004, MS-DES-0010, and the retrieval-layer codebase, `Market` (capitalized) refers to the Skill Market service — the same proper-noun pattern as `Cowork` or `Claude`. A heading like `### Alternative E — wait indefinitely for the Market owner` was getting sentence-case-lowercased to `... market owner` by Rule 3.1 because `market` wasn't registered. Covered by **1 new unit test** (`test_rule_3_1_preserves_market_as_proper_noun`) — 48 tests total in `test_style_autofix.py`, all passing. The style-guide reference doc already points at `PROPER_NOUNS` as the authoritative source (Rule 3.1 prose), so no reference-doc edit is needed. Consistent with the prior Phase 3 palette-cleanser widenings (HTML heading tags, language/locale adjectives) — when sweeping or writing new docs surfaces a real proper noun gap, the fix is a `PROPER_NOUNS` entry plus a regression test.
- **Doc-freshness relevance v2 — BM25-weighted importance scoring and priority-digest output (`skills/doc-freshness/scripts/doc_importance.py` (new), `skills/doc-freshness/scripts/doc_freshness_scanner.py`, `skills/doc-freshness/SKILL.md`)** — three concentric additive changes per MS-DES-0009 that target the `doc-freshness` skill's 38% utilization (run #13 scorecard) by moving it from "ran it once and stopped" toward "ran it weekly and acted on output." (1) New `doc_importance.py` module exports `compute_importance_scores(docs_root, doc_paths) -> dict[str, float]`. Internally it ports `_tokenize` and a simplified `DocBm25Index` from `core/skill/retrieval/local_bm25_recall.py` (stdlib-only; preserves `BM25_K1=1.2`, `BM25_B=0.75`, `MIN_TOKEN_LENGTH=2`, and the upstream stopword set — the port is deliberate to preserve the self-contained-script invariant under `skills/*/scripts/`, with upstream-source comments for a future shared-primitives consolidation). Each doc's `importance_score` is a max-normalized convex combination of *distinctive content density* (sum of top-`K=10` term IDFs, `W_INTRINSIC=0.6`) and *inbound reference authority* (count of other docs linking to it, `W_REFERENCE=0.4`), clamped to `[0.0, 1.0]`. A `classify_priority` helper discretizes the continuous score into three buckets at tertile-inspired cut-points (`0.66` → `high`, `0.33` → `medium`, else `low`). (2) Scanner integration: every record in `docs[]` gains `importance_score` and `priority` sibling fields, and the summary block gains `priority_counts: {"high", "medium", "low"}` counting docs per bucket. No existing field is removed or renamed — full JSON backward compatibility for any consumer. (3) Two new CLI flags: `--min-priority {low,medium,high}` (default `low` = pass-through) filters the returned list to at-or-above the given priority with all summary counters recomputing against the filtered list; and `--format {json,priority-digest}` (default `json`) adds a concise Markdown-digest output mode with an H2 per non-empty priority bucket and a single-line summary per doc (no full commit listings), tailored for weekly review. SKILL.md gains a **Step 2a — weekly-rhythm recommendation** describing the intended flow: `--since "7 days ago" --min-priority medium --format priority-digest` → read the digest → act on the top two or three → repeat next week. Covered by **26 new unit tests** (`skills/doc-freshness/scripts/test_doc_importance.py`) — 5 tokenizer-parity tests (English, CJK, mixed script, empty input, short-tokens-dropped) locking the port against upstream divergence, 4 BM25 index invariants (empty corpus, IDF monotonic in rarity, top-k ordering, single-doc IDF finiteness), 5 `compute_importance_scores` invariants (empty → `{}`, single-doc → `1.0`, unit-interval bound, max-normalization, weights-sum-to-1.0), 5 inbound-reference-counting cases (Markdown links, inline-code paths, self-reference exclusion, anchor stripping, external-URL exclusion), 3 priority-bucket boundary tests, and 4 scanner-integration tests against a tmp-dir git fixture (new fields present per record, `--min-priority` shrinks the list, JSON backward compat, priority-digest formatter emits valid Markdown with no JSON noise). All 26 pass in ~53ms; the pre-existing 20 `test_relevance.py` tests continue to pass unchanged. Five rejected alternatives documented in the design spec: log-driven retrieval-frequency (no log source exists today), extending the skill-BM25 index to include docs (field-weighting assumptions are wrong for docs), precomputed `docs/.doc-importance.json` cache (drift risk, scan is already fast enough), sort-by-staleness (doesn't differentiate central vs. forgotten docs), and continuous `priority_rank` integer (order-sensitivity + false-precision). Design spec at [`docs/design/doc-freshness-relevance-v2-bm25-weighting.md`](docs/design/doc-freshness-relevance-v2-bm25-weighting.md) (MS-DES-0009). Closes Phase 3 candidate #8 from the interim retrospective.
- **Changelog-writer conventional-commit scope surfacing (`skills/changelog-writer/scripts/git_log_parser.py`, `skills/changelog-writer/SKILL.md`)** — three narrow changes per MS-DES-0008 that close a long-standing gap where the parser extracted conventional-commit scopes but never surfaced them to consumers. (1) The `summary` block gains a `scopes_used` field — a sorted list of unique non-null, non-empty scope strings across the returned commits; always present (may be `[]`). (2) A new repeatable `--filter-scope <scope>` CLI flag (and corresponding `filter_scopes=` kwarg on `parse_git_log`) narrows the commit list to scopes matching case-insensitively and exact-match, with OR-semantics across repeated values. The summary counters (`total_commits`, `authors`, `date_range`, `scopes_used`) recompute against the filtered list so downstream consumers never see inconsistent numbers. (3) SKILL.md gains a "Step 3a — Scope-based grouping" sub-step showing how to use `scopes_used` to organize a changelog with bolded-scope bullets under each Keep a Changelog category. Covered by **14 new unit tests** (`skills/changelog-writer/scripts/test_git_log_parser.py`) — 10 for `parse_conventional` edge cases (bare type, type+scope, type+breaking, type+scope+breaking, uppercase type, hyphenated scope, slash-in-scope, trailing whitespace, uncategorized subject, BREAKING CHANGE in subject) plus 2 for `scopes_used` aggregation and 2 for `filter_scopes=` / `--filter-scope`. All passing in ~1ms via stdlib `unittest` + `unittest.mock.patch.object` — no pytest, no real git repo required. Design spec at [`docs/design/changelog-writer-scope-extraction.md`](docs/design/changelog-writer-scope-extraction.md) (MS-DES-0008). Closes Phase 3 candidate #7 from the interim retrospective.
- **Analyzer `current_warnings_backlog` accessor fix (`skills/doc-pipeline/scripts/analyze_pipeline_log.py`)** — the metric used to walk the run list in reverse looking for the most recent *non-zero* remaining-warnings count, which meant a run that cleared the backlog to zero was invisible to the analyzer and the reported backlog "stuck" at the prior non-zero value. The accessor now takes the last attributed style-checker run's `style_warnings_remaining` value directly (including explicit zero), falling back to `0` only when no style-checker run has ever been attributed. This correctly reports `backlog: 0` after run #13's README sweep cleared the Rule 3.1 findings. Covered by **2 new regression tests** in `test_analyze_pipeline_log.py` (50 total, all passing): one locking in that an explicit-zero latest run is respected, and one covering the no-style-checker-ever-attributed edge case. Post-fix baseline captured at [`docs/analysis/pipeline-log-baseline-2026-04-14-readme-swept.md`](docs/analysis/pipeline-log-baseline-2026-04-14-readme-swept.md) (MS-ANA-0002).
- **Style-guide meta-fix and PROPER_NOUNS widening (`skills/style-checker/references/style-guide.md`, `skills/style-checker/scripts/style_autofix.py`)** — the style guide itself was failing Rule 3.1 in 44 of its own headings (a visible embarrassment documented in the Phase 3 interim retrospective). Applied the autofixer in a single sweep, leaving only three intentional findings (two Rule 4.1 four-backtick-fence demonstrations and one Rule 7.1 "click here" Bad example) where the text is example content rather than a real violation. The sweep surfaced two PROPER_NOUNS gaps that were fixed as sub-work:
  - **HTML heading-level tags** (`h1`…`h6`): the `_is_acronym` helper only detects pure-alpha all-caps, so `H1`…`H6` (which contain a digit) were being lowercased. Added explicit entries to `PROPER_NOUNS` with an inline comment documenting the `_is_acronym` limitation.
  - **Language and locale proper nouns** (`Latin`, `American`, `English`, `British`, `Unicode`): not technology acronyms but still proper nouns that should not be sentence-case-lowercased mid-heading. Added to `PROPER_NOUNS` as a labeled sub-section.
  Covered by **2 new unit tests** (`test_style_autofix.py`: 47 total, all passing): `test_rule_3_1_preserves_html_heading_level_tags` and `test_rule_3_1_preserves_language_and_locale_proper_nouns`.
- **Rule 3.1 sentence-case hardening (`skills/style-checker/scripts/style_autofix.py`)** — two targeted fixes to close the two failure modes documented in the Phase 2 retrospective: (1) `PROPER_NOUNS` registry widened from ~30 to ~60 entries, organized with category comments and an authoritative-source reference in the style guide. Additions include `OpenClaw`, `SQLite`, `PostgreSQL`, `MySQL`, `iOS`, `Flet`, `Briefcase`, `Pydantic`, `SQLAlchemy`, plus the acronym block (`API`, `CLI`, `SDK`, `UI`, `IDE`, `GUI`, `OSS`, `BSD`, `MIT`, `TLS`, `HTTP`, `HTTPS`, `URL`, `AST`, `NFKC`, `RRF`). (2) `_sentence_case_heading` now threads an `at_sentence_start` state variable that flips `True` after any token whose trailing punctuation is exactly one of `.`, `!`, `?` — excluding ellipses (`...`) and technical identifiers (`v0.3.0`, `config.json`). Multi-sentence headings like `## One Repo. One Learning Agent.` now correctly produce `## One repo. One learning agent.` Covered by **12 new unit tests** (45 total in `test_style_autofix.py`, all passing in ~80ms), including registry invariants (every value starts uppercase, `openclaw` entry present) and five sentence-boundary cases (period, question mark, exclamation mark, ellipsis-as-non-terminator, version-literal-as-non-terminator). Applied against `README.md` in a single sweep — 21 headings canonicalized, `--check` now reports clean. Style-guide Rule 3.1 prose extended with a multi-sentence-headings subsection and a proper-nouns subsection pointing at the `PROPER_NOUNS` dict as the canonical source. Design spec at [`docs/design/rule-3-1-proper-nouns-and-sentence-boundaries.md`](docs/design/rule-3-1-proper-nouns-and-sentence-boundaries.md) (MS-DES-0007). Post-sweep baseline captured at [`docs/analysis/pipeline-log-baseline-2026-04-14-readme-swept.md`](docs/analysis/pipeline-log-baseline-2026-04-14-readme-swept.md). Closes Phase 3 candidate #1 from the Phase 2 retrospective.
- **Pipeline-log utility-scoring analyzer (`skills/doc-pipeline/scripts/analyze_pipeline_log.py`)** — stdlib-only Python 3.11+ read-only analyzer that reads `docs/.doc-pipeline-log.json`, classifies each run by which underlying skill was invoked using a conservative attribution heuristic (documented rules keyed by skill in a single top-level `ATTRIBUTION_RULES` dict), and emits a per-skill scorecard as human-readable text, machine-readable JSON, or a drop-in Markdown table. Metrics are grouped into three families: per-skill (utilization rate, coverage, runs-invoked list), skill-specific numerics (style-checker `total_errors_fixed` + mean + max + current warnings backlog; doc-freshness scan totals + fresh rate; changelog-writer edits + version-stamp events; release-notes created; doc-generator API-ref touches; doc-pipeline runs logged), and overall (docs-first discipline rate from `MS-DES-NNNN` references, release cadence from tightened `vX.Y.Z release` or `release cut` regex, log span, longest gap). Three output modes via `--format {human,json,markdown}`. Covered by **48 unit tests** (`skills/doc-pipeline/scripts/test_analyze_pipeline_log.py`) — stdlib `unittest`, no pytest dependency, all passing in ~7ms, with separate test classes covering attribution per skill, metric arithmetic on a three-run fixture log, the three output formatters, and the empty-log edge case. Design spec at [`docs/design/pipeline-log-analyzer.md`](docs/design/pipeline-log-analyzer.md) (MS-DES-0006). Baseline run against the real 11-run log captured at [`docs/analysis/pipeline-log-baseline-2026-04-14.md`](docs/analysis/pipeline-log-baseline-2026-04-14.md). Closes Phase 3 candidate #3 from the Phase 2 retrospective.
- **Release-version drift checker (`build_scripts/check_release_versions.py`)** — stdlib-only Python 3.11+ script that reads the canonical release version from `pyproject.toml [project].version` and verifies every other place the version appears in the repo matches it. Ships with a declarative registry of the ten known call sites (three `pyproject.toml` entries including the Flet and Briefcase packagers, `version.py`, `middleware/config/system_config.json`, and the five hard-coded Python-literal fallbacks in `cli/main.py`, `bootstrap.py`, `middleware/storage/schemas.py`, `middleware/storage/models.py`, `gui/modules/auto_update_manager.py`). Emits human-readable or `--json` drift reports; exits `0` on clean, `1` on drift, `2` on usage error. Covered by **12 unit tests** (`build_scripts/test_check_release_versions.py`) — stdlib `unittest`, no pytest dependency, all passing in ~7ms against isolated tmp-dir fixture repos. Design spec at [`docs/design/release-checklist-script.md`](docs/design/release-checklist-script.md) (MS-DES-0005). Closes Phase 3 candidate #5 from the Phase 2 retrospective.

## [0.3.0] - 2026-04-14

Internal-tooling release. Introduces a BM25 lexical retrieval layer that fuses
with the existing vector pipeline via reciprocal rank fusion, a six-skill
tech-writing suite (plus orchestrator) with an MS-DES-NNNN design-spec
convention, and a `docs/.doc-pipeline-log.json` feedback loop for tracking
every doc-pipeline run over time. Architecture baseline from v0.2.0 is
preserved.

### Added

- **BM25 lexical retrieval layer (`LocalBm25Recall`)** — a third local recall strategy at `core/skill/retrieval/local_bm25_recall.py` that runs a pure-Python BM25 search over skill names, descriptions, and full SKILL.md bodies. Stdlib-only (no `rank_bm25`, no `whoosh`, no `nltk`). Field-weighting by token repetition (`W_NAME=4`, `W_DESC=2`, `W_BODY=1`), canonical BM25 parameters (`k1=1.2`, `b=0.75`), NFKC-normalized Unicode-aware tokenizer, and a ~30-word English stopword set. The index lives in memory, rebuilds lazily on the first query after construction, and auto-invalidates when the skills directory's signature changes. Covers queries where lexical precision matters (exact names, tool IDs, body-only keywords) that the vector pipeline can miss. Design spec at [`docs/design/bm25-retrieval-layer.md`](docs/design/bm25-retrieval-layer.md). Closes Phase 2 candidate #6 from the retrospective.
- **Hybrid score fusion via reciprocal rank fusion (RRF)** in `MultiRecall._rerank_candidates` — when the same skill surfaces in both the BM25 and the vector strategy's output, the two per-strategy ranks are fused into a single score via `RRF(skill) = 1/(60 + rank_bm25) + 1/(60 + rank_vec)` (Cormack, Clarke & Büttcher 2009). Chosen over linear-combination fusion because RRF needs no score normalization and no tunable `α`. The local-before-remote tier rule is preserved: remote candidates can never rank above any local candidate regardless of fused score. Hybrid hits are tagged with `match_type="hybrid"` for diagnostics.
- **Extended `RecallCandidate` schema** — four new optional fields (`bm25_score`, `vector_score`, `bm25_rank`, `vector_rank`) feed the fusion stage and surface per-strategy diagnostics. All default to `None` and are ignored by callers that only read `name` / `score`, so nothing downstream had to change.
- **`LocalBm25Recall` unit tests** at `tests/test_skills/retrieval/test_local_bm25_recall.py` — tokenizer behavior (NFKC, stopwords, CJK, underscores, digits), index build/score/rank invariants, field-weighting, body-only-keyword surfacing, idempotent rebuild, empty-query handling, directory-signature invalidation, deterministic output, and tuning-constant guard-rails. Plus fusion unit tests in `tests/test_skills/retrieval/test_multi_recall.py` covering `_stamp_rank`, `_merge_into_existing`, and `_apply_fusion` including the AC #14 cross-list-vs-single-list inequality.
- **`doc-generator` translation-pass detection and annotation** — `skills/doc-generator/scripts/extract_signatures.py` now classifies every docstring (module-level, class, method, function) by Unicode script and reports the result as new sibling fields `docstring_language` (one of `target` / `non_target` / `mixed` / `empty` / `unknown`) and `docstring_scripts` (sorted list of detected scripts). The top-level JSON summary gains a `docstring_language_counts` block. Two new CLI flags: `--target-script` (default `latin`; accepts any of the 18 supported Unicode scripts) and `--translation-summary-only` (prints a human-readable tally and exits without emitting the full JSON). `skills/doc-generator/SKILL.md` gains a **Step 2.5 — translation pass** that walks the agent through translating flagged docstrings while preserving originals as `<!-- Original (han): ... -->` HTML comments and emitting a "Translation summary" callout at the top of the generated doc. Stdlib-only (`unicodedata`), no third-party dependencies. Covered by **28 unit tests** (`skills/doc-generator/scripts/test_language_classifier.py`), all passing. Design spec at [`docs/design/doc-generator-translation-pass.md`](docs/design/doc-generator-translation-pass.md). Closes Phase 2 candidate #5 from the retrospective.
- **Module-level docstring extraction for Python source** — the extractor now emits a `module_docstring` field (plus sibling `module_docstring_language` / `module_docstring_scripts`) for every file. Previously the extractor only walked classes, functions, and constants, so file-level prose was dropped. C# and TypeScript extractors emit `module_docstring: null` for schema symmetry.
- **`style-checker` auto-fix script (`skills/style-checker/scripts/style_autofix.py`)** — deterministic, line-oriented Python implementation of the six mechanical style-guide rules (3.1, 3.2, 3.6, 4.1, 6.1, 7.1). Stdlib-only, no third-party dependencies. Supports `--check` (CI gating, non-zero exit on violation), `--dry-run` (prints a unified diff), `--rules` / `--ignore-rules` (selective application), `--verbose`, and `--json`. Fence-aware and MDX front-matter-aware: content inside fenced code blocks and YAML front matter is passed through verbatim. Covered by **34 unit tests** (`skills/style-checker/scripts/test_style_autofix.py`), all passing. Design spec at [`docs/design/style-checker-autofix-script.md`](docs/design/style-checker-autofix-script.md). Closes Phase 2 candidate #4 from the retrospective.
- **`--include-untracked` flag on the doc-freshness scanner** — opt-in mode that scans Markdown files not yet committed to Git. Untracked files appear in the output with `tracked: false` and a `last_updated` derived from filesystem `mtime` rather than `git log`. Useful during drafting; leave off for release-time audits. Documented in `skills/doc-freshness/SKILL.md`; covered by 3 new integration tests in `skills/doc-freshness/scripts/test_relevance.py` (20 tests total, all passing).
- **Style guide Rule 3.6 — "No trailing colons on headings"** (WARNING, auto-fixable). Colons at the end of Markdown headings are redundant with the heading syntax itself, clutter auto-generated anchors, and hurt scannability. The `style-checker` now strips them automatically.
- **Style guide Rule 9.1 — "MDX front matter"** (WARNING, not auto-fixed). `.mdx` files should declare at minimum `title` and `description` in their YAML front-matter block. Generating a sensible `description` requires understanding the doc's purpose, so the checker flags omissions rather than synthesizing values.
- **Tech-writing skill suite** — six Cowork-format skills for documentation
  work, plus an orchestrator (c41aa41):
  - `style-checker` — knowledge skill that reviews Markdown against a
    30-rule style guide (`skills/style-checker/references/style-guide.md`)
    and auto-fixes mechanical issues while flagging judgment calls.
  - `changelog-writer` — hybrid skill that parses conventional-commit git
    history via `scripts/git_log_parser.py` and categorizes entries into
    Keep a Changelog sections.
  - `doc-freshness` — hybrid skill whose `scripts/doc_freshness_scanner.py`
    scans a `docs/` tree against git history and classifies each file as
    fresh / possibly_stale / likely_stale.
  - `doc-generator` — hybrid skill that extracts signatures from Python
    (AST-based), C#, and TypeScript (regex-based) via
    `scripts/extract_signatures.py`, with reference, configuration, and
    getting-started templates.
  - `release-notes` — knowledge skill for audience-calibrated release notes
    (developer / end-user / ops / executive) with tone examples.
  - `doc-pipeline` — orchestrator that runs the other five in sequence,
    logs results to `docs/.doc-pipeline-log.json`, and works around the
    framework's no-skill-to-skill-invocation constraint by invoking
    sibling scripts directly.
- **Tech-writing adaptation plan** at `docs/tech-writing-adaptation-plan.md`
  — phased plan for adapting Memento-Skills' skill-learning loop to
  technical-writing workflows (c41aa41).
- **Pipeline feedback log** at `docs/.doc-pipeline-log.json` — seed of a
  utility-scoring feedback loop for tracking pipeline runs over time
  (c41aa41).
- **`docs/design/`** — design-note directory for tech-writing-skill
  changes. First entry: `doc-freshness-relevance-filter.md`.
- **`skills/doc-freshness/scripts/test_relevance.py`** — 17-test suite for
  the relevance filter. Runs via `python test_relevance.py`; no pytest
  dependency.
- **Phase 1 retrospective** at `docs/phase-1-retrospective.md`.
- **First-pass API reference** at `docs/api/skill-gateway.md`, generated
  from `core/skill/gateway.py` by the `doc-generator` skill.
- **Test fixture** at `test-fixtures/columnviewwidth.mdx` — auto-fixed
  output from a `style-checker` run against external input.

### Changed

- **`doc-freshness` relevance filter rewritten** — replaced the fuzzy
  substring heuristic with directory-prefix path overlap. Backtick-quoted
  topics and commit subjects are no longer matched; only commit files that
  overlap with paths the doc explicitly references count as "related
  changes." Fixes the false-positive pattern documented in
  `docs/.doc-pipeline-log.json` where meta-commits to `skills/` or
  `docs/` flagged unrelated design docs. See
  `docs/design/doc-freshness-relevance-filter.md` for rationale. Verified
  by `skills/doc-freshness/scripts/test_relevance.py` (17 tests).

## [0.2.0] - 2026-03-31

Major architecture upgrade. Introduces Bounded Context boundaries across the
agent and skill subsystems, a three-layer configuration model, a cloud Skill
Market, and a cross-platform IM Gateway.

### Added

- **Skill Market** — cloud search, download, and auto-install flow for sharing
  skills across installations (f05f9bc).
- **Multi-platform IM Gateway** — unified messaging layer spanning Feishu,
  DingTalk, WeCom, and WeChat, each with its own adapter under `3rd/` (f05f9bc).
- **`im-platform` built-in skill** — exposes the IM Gateway to agents as a
  first-class skill (f05f9bc).
- **GUI workspace browser** — visual session and skill management UI alongside
  the existing CLI (f05f9bc).
- **Test suite, build scripts, and bootstrap entry point** — `bootstrap.py`,
  `build_scripts/`, and CI workflow under `.github/workflows/build.yml` to
  standardize packaging and verification (f05f9bc).

### Changed

- **BREAKING: Bounded Context architecture redesign** — the agent and skill
  modules were re-partitioned into explicit bounded contexts. Public module
  layouts under `core/` changed; integrations that import internals will need
  to be re-pointed (f05f9bc).
- **BREAKING: Configuration system v2** — three-layer isolation across System,
  User, and Runtime scopes. Existing single-file configurations must be
  migrated into the new layered layout (f05f9bc).
- **Execution engine refactor** — adds a Tool Bridge abstraction, policy hooks,
  richer error recovery, and a loop-detection guard around the ReAct loop
  (f05f9bc).
- README rewritten for the v0.2.0 release (f05f9bc, c8f91b6, adc2080).

## [0.1.0] - 2026-03-19

### Added

- Initial public commit of Memento-Skills — ReAct-based agent core, skill
  gateway, and the first pass of built-in skills (52c75eb).
